title: Coroutines
objectives: Write async code with suspend functions

sections.markdown: Kotlin coroutines are lightweight, suspendable computations for asynchronous code that reads sequentially. A suspend function can pause without blocking a thread.

sections.code:
viewModelScope.launch {              // structured: tied to ViewModel
  val user = withContext(Dispatchers.IO) { api.getUser() } // off main
  _state.value = user                 // back on main automatically
}

sections.markdown: **Structured concurrency**: coroutines launched in a scope (viewModelScope, lifecycleScope) are automatically cancelled when the scope ends — no leaked work after a screen closes. This is a key advantage over raw callbacks/threads.
Doing blocking I/O on Dispatchers.Main (freezes the UI), or collecting a Flow without a lifecycle-aware collector (repeatOnLifecycle), which wastes work while the UI is in the background.
Flow is the coroutine-native reactive stream. Use StateFlow for UI state and collect it with repeatOnLifecycle(STARTED) so collection pauses when the screen isn't visible.

flashcards.back: The function can pause and resume without blocking its thread.
Coroutines are bound to a scope and auto-cancelled when it ends, preventing leaks.
